title: Awesome Agentic Use Cases: verified agentic AI use cases with evals, measured cost, and observed failure modes
description:
A collection of agentic AI use cases in which every entry ships with the harness that verifies it, rather than a demonstration that it ran once.

Each use case must clear a fixed bar before it is included: it runs from a clean clone with a single command and no API key; it has at least 20 scenarios with programmatic ground truth generated from a committed seed; cost per run is computed in dollars from measured token usage rather than estimated; results are reported across at least three repeated runs with paired bootstrap confidence intervals, because agent runs are stochastic and a single run is noise; and at least three failure modes are documented that were observed in a committed run rather than hypothesised.

Version 0.1.0 contains 13 use cases across 7 industries, 55 real-model evaluations, 72 observed failure modes, and 208 tests, with continuous integration exercising every use case. It also contains a cross-cutting taxonomy that groups the observed failures into 11 recurring patterns with measured incidence, several of which were found independently in eight different domains.

Every result records its own provenance: the time it ran, the harness version, the interpreter, and the model the provider actually served. Results obtained against floating model aliases are labelled as point-in-time observations rather than presented as exactly reproducible.

Limitations. The worlds are synthetic. This is a deliberate trade: it buys exact programmatic ground truth, so scoring is exact rather than a judge model's opinion, and it lets any published number be reproduced at zero cost on free model tiers. It does not support claims about production traffic, and a domain expert writing different rules would obtain different numbers. Sample sizes are 30 scenarios by 3 repeats per model, so confidence intervals are wide and are reported rather than omitted.
